title: How to Get Your Org to Adopt Coding Agents (Without Shipping Garbage) — Eyal Blum, Figma
talk_summary: Figma's engineer describes uneven coding-agent adoption and argues quality comes from investing in verification, deterministic checks, TDD, and detailed plans with independently verifiable phases. He also emphasizes attention-aware AI/human communication and using skeptical senior engineers' feedback as the roadmap for guardrails.

takeaways.what_they_do: Shift verification from humans to agents and deterministic checks; when an agent finds a useful check, encode it as a repeatable test or flow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: investing in verification is probably the highest value thing we can do in our code base

takeaways.what_they_do: Write a detailed plan with a why/executive summary, split into small PR-sized phases, each with its own validation gate before the next phase.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Make sure that the plan can be broken down into small parts that can each be verified independently.
takeaways.numbers: ~20 PRs, mostly 10-100 lines; ~5x speedup (six weeks coding in one week)

takeaways.what_they_do: Have the agent write a failing test first, then implement until it passes, so tests define the goal rather than being fitted to code afterward.
takeaways.evidence_quote: red to green to red to green at the TDD style, it almost always gives you better results

takeaways.what_they_do: Move review checks down to lint/compiler/unit tests, use agent review for encoded architectural standards, and reserve humans for functionality and whether it is the right thing to build.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Move as much as you can down to the deterministic analysis

takeaways.what_they_do: PR descriptions start with a short hand-written intent summary, then labeled AI-generated details, so readers know what to trust and where to focus.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every PR description will start with something like that, something that I wrote by hand

takeaways.what_they_do: Bring skeptical senior engineers in and treat their complaints as the roadmap for validation gaps and agent-codebase interaction improvements.
takeaways.evidence_quote: their feedback is basically the road map of how to improve your agent interacting with the code base
